everyday.label: Everyday Explainer
everyday.who: General public, customers, students — no tech background
everyday.goal: Awareness and trust: make a big tech shift feel understandable and relevant to daily life
everyday.business_value: Reach and audience growth; positions Prakash as the trusted explainer
everyday.voice: Professional documentary narrator: clear, warm, brisk; explains like a BBC presenter. Delivery comes from the brand voice settings, not from tags.
writing: No acronyms or jargon; if a term is unavoidable, explain it in the same sentence
Open with a relatable everyday moment (shopping on a phone, a delivery at the door)
One idea per scene; short sentences; analogies from daily life
Name brands people know only in narration (ChatGPT, Gemini), never as copied interfaces
End with what it means for the viewer and one simple question
everyday.visuals: Mostly real-life footage and recorded screens that show exactly what is said; simple stats; avoid architecture diagrams
everyday.cta: Ask a simple personal question (Would you let an AI shop for you?)
everyday.platforms: YouTube + LinkedIn long version; Reels/Shorts/X clips

business.label: Business Leaders
business.who: Heads of operations, marketing, sales, product; non-technical executives
business.goal: Show what changes for customers, revenue and teams, and what to ask their tech team
business.voice: Professional business presenter: confident, clear, brisk. Delivery comes from the brand voice settings, not from tags.
writing: Translate every tech idea into a customer, revenue or cost effect
At most one technical term per scene, explained
Use real company examples and numbers
Close with 3 questions to ask your tech team
business.visuals: Footage of customers, stores and screens + simple charts and comparisons; at most one simplified diagram
business.cta: Ask which part of their customer journey they'd change first
business.platforms: LinkedIn first; YouTube; clips on X and Instagram

boardroom.label: Boardroom
boardroom.who: CEOs, boards, CFOs, investors and PE operating partners
boardroom.goal: Risk, cost, ROI and the decision to make now — in the time a board slot allows
boardroom.voice: Executive presenting a proposal to a board: measured, confident, concise. Delivery comes from the brand voice settings, not from tags.
writing: Lead with the business risk or opportunity and its size
Frame as decisions, trade-offs, cost of waiting
Numbers with sources; no technical detail beyond one sentence
Close with the one decision for the next board meeting
boardroom.visuals: Stats, decision cards, timelines, a few premium footage shots (boardrooms, markets, customers)
boardroom.cta: What decision would you put on your next board agenda?

tech.label: Tech Leaders
tech.who: CTOs, CIOs, VPs of Engineering, enterprise and solution architects
tech.goal: Patterns, target architecture, trade-offs and a roadmap
tech.business_value: Architecture consulting; credibility with technical hiring managers
tech.voice: IT executive presenting a use case: authoritative, precise, brisk. Delivery comes from the brand voice settings, not from tags.
writing: Technical terms are fine; name protocols and patterns
Show the target architecture and the trade-offs
Give a phased roadmap
tech.visuals: Diagrams, flows, comparisons; footage only for context
tech.cta: Ask how their stack handles the problem today

founders.label: Founders & SMB
founders.who: Startup founders and owners of small and mid-size businesses
founders.goal: What to do this quarter with a small team and budget
founders.voice: Experienced advisor: practical, direct, energetic. Delivery comes from the brand voice settings, not from tags.
writing: Concrete steps, tools and rough costs
Small-business examples
What to do first, what to ignore
Plain language; one technical term per scene at most
founders.visuals: Small-business footage (shops, warehouses, laptops), recorded screens, checklists
founders.cta: Invite them to share their business and situation; offer a free first conversation

leadership.label: Leadership Lens
leadership.who: Future employers: CEOs, boards and executive recruiters; also senior peers
leadership.goal: Show how Prakash thinks and leads: point of view, transformation stories, team building
leadership.business_value: Leadership roles; board and advisory seats
leadership.voice: Leader telling a story: calm authority, first person, sincere. Delivery comes from the brand voice settings, not from tags.
writing: First person (I, my teams)
Story structure: situation, decision, outcome, lesson
No client names or confidential details
One clear leadership principle per video
leadership.visuals: More @me Flow clips across the 8 angles; office and team footage; quote cards
leadership.cta: Ask leaders how they handle the same situation

academy.label: Architect's Academy
academy.who: Engineers and developers growing into architect roles
academy.goal: Teach one concept properly with worked examples
academy.business_value: YouTube audience growth and community; talent pipeline
academy.voice: Senior architect teaching: clear, patient, structured. Delivery comes from the brand voice settings, not from tags.
writing: Define each term, then use it
Worked example from a familiar app
Common mistakes and how to avoid them
Homework or next step
academy.visuals: Step-by-step diagrams, timelines, recorded screens of tools; whiteboard-style
academy.cta: Ask viewers to try it and share their design
academy.platforms: YouTube first; LinkedIn; clips on X
